title: The Hidden Cost of Waiting: Why Coverage Hurdles Stall Necessary Patient Care
excerpt: With 95% of physicians reporting that prior authorization delays access to essential clinical care, healthcare practices must rethink workflows to protect patient outcomes and revenue.
seoTitle: Prior Authorization Delays: AMA Survey Findings & Practice Solutions
seoDescription: Explore why 95% of physicians report prior authorization delays necessary care, and discover actionable revenue cycle strategies to overcome payer obstacles.
content:
Why Prior Authorization Has Become a Patient-Care Problem

Prior authorization was meant to control costs. In practice, it has become one of the biggest reasons patients wait for care they already need. When 95% of physicians say authorization delays access to essential treatment, this is no longer just an administrative issue — it is a clinical risk.

The Real Cost of Waiting

Delays lead to missed treatments, worsening conditions, abandoned care plans, and extra work for front-desk and billing teams. Practices lose revenue from cancelled appointments, rework, and denied claims, while patients lose trust.

What Practices Can Do

  • Verify authorization requirements before the visit, not after
  • Track every authorization with status, payer, and deadline
  • Build payer-specific checklists for high-denial services
  • Appeal quickly with complete clinical documentation
  • Use a centralized RCM workflow so nothing falls through the cracks

At Hima Tech RCM, we help practices reduce authorization delays with proactive verification, clean documentation, and disciplined follow-up — so patients get care on time and practices get paid on time.

content:
What Is Margin Compression?

Practices are earning the same or less per visit, while staffing, technology, and compliance costs keep rising. That squeeze is margin compression — and administrative work is one of its biggest drivers.

Why In-House Billing Struggles

Small in-house teams face turnover, training gaps, and bottlenecks during peak claim volumes. One absent biller can delay an entire week of claims.

The Remote Billing Advantage

  • Lower overhead than hiring, training, and managing in-house
  • Faster claim submission and denial follow-up
  • Specialized expertise in payer rules and coding
  • Scalable support during growth or seasonal spikes

title: 7 Ways to Reduce Medical Billing Denials
excerpt: Discover seven actionable strategies to minimize claim rejections, streamline clinical documentation, and safeguard reimbursement cash flow for healthcare practices.
seoTitle: 7 Ways to Reduce Medical Billing Denials | Revenue Cycle Guide
seoDescription: Explore practical steps to decrease claim rejections, improve front-desk verification, and optimize cash flow in your medical practice.
content:
1. Verify Eligibility Before Every Visit

Most preventable denials start at the front desk. Verify coverage, benefits, and authorization requirements before the patient arrives.

2. Get Documentation Right the First Time

Clean claims need complete, specific documentation that supports medical necessity and correct coding.

3. Code With Specificity

Use the most specific ICD-10 and CPT codes available. Unspecified codes are a common denial trigger.

4. Submit Claims Quickly

Do not wait for month-end. Submit daily and track timely-filing deadlines by payer.

5. Work Denials Every Day

Denials are not dead claims. Categorize them by root cause, appeal within payer windows, and fix the workflow that caused them.

6. Track Your Denial Rate

If you do not measure it, you cannot fix it. Watch denial rate, days in A/R, and first-pass resolution rate.

7. Partner With RCM Experts

title: Preparing Your Practice for ICD-10 Changes in 2027
excerpt: Explore key shifts in diagnostic specificity, revenue cycle risks, and EHR preparation strategies for healthcare providers approaching the 2027 coding updates.
seoTitle: ICD-10 Updates 2027: Provider Guide to Coding & Billing Shifts
seoDescription: Prepare your practice for ICD-10 updates in 2027. Learn how specificity changes, payer scrutiny, and documentation audits impact clinical revenue cycles.
content:
What Changes in 2027?

ICD-10 updates bring new, revised, and deleted codes, plus tighter expectations for specificity. Practices that keep coding the old way will see more denials and audits.

3 Areas to Prepare Now

1. EHR & Encoder Updates

Confirm your EHR, clearinghouse, and encoder will be updated before October 1. Test claims in advance.

2. Documentation

Train providers to document laterality, severity, encounter type, and causal relationships — payers expect it.

3. Denial Monitoring

Watch for new denial patterns in the first 60 days after go-live and fix them fast.

title: When Do FY 2027 ICD-10-PCS Updates Go Into Effect?
excerpt: FY 2027 ICD-10-PCS updates go into effect on October 1, 2026. Learn what hospitals and inpatient coders must update before the go-live date.
seoTitle: When Do FY 2027 ICD-10-PCS Updates Go Into Effect? Effective Date Guide
seoDescription: FY 2027 ICD-10-PCS updates take effect October 1, 2026. Learn the effective date, new procedure codes, and hospital preparation checklist.
content:
Short Answer: October 1, 2026

FY 2027 ICD-10-PCS updates go into effect on October 1, 2026 for discharges on or after that date. This is the federal fiscal year start, and CMS applies the new PCS code set from that day forward.

What Is ICD-10-PCS?

ICD-10-PCS is the procedure coding system used for inpatient hospital procedures in the United States. Unlike ICD-10-CM (diagnoses), PCS codes describe what was done, how it was done, and with what approach and device.

What to Update Before October 1

  • Update your encoder, EHR, and grouper to the FY 2027 PCS version
  • Review new and deleted PCS codes that affect your top procedures
  • Train inpatient coders on new root operations, approaches, and devices
  • Test claims with the new code set before go-live
  • Watch for MS-DRG shifts caused by procedure-code changes

Common Mistake to Avoid

Do not use FY 2027 PCS codes for discharges before October 1, 2026, and do not use FY 2026 codes after. The discharge date controls which code set applies.

title: ICD-10 Coding Pitfalls: Avoiding Compliance Risk
excerpt: Learn the common ICD-10 coding mistakes that can lead to denials, audits, compliance risks, and lost revenue.
seoTitle: ICD-10 Coding Pitfalls: Avoiding Compliance Risk | Hima Tech RCM
seoDescription: Avoid the most common ICD-10 coding mistakes. Learn how unspecified codes, poor documentation, and outdated code sets create denials and audit risk.
content:
The Most Common ICD-10 Pitfalls

  • Unspecified codes: Using unspecified codes when the record supports a more specific code
  • Copy-forward errors: Copying old diagnoses that are no longer active
  • Missing laterality and severity: Leaving out details payers now require
  • Wrong 7th character: Incorrect encounter type for injuries and fractures
  • Outdated code sets: Coding with last year's codes after October 1

How to Stay Compliant

Audit charts regularly, train providers on documentation, and fix patterns — not just single claims. A small coding error repeated 100 times becomes a compliance problem.
